head: pr17488-r25
report:
Environment issue (tmp dir didn't exist). Rerunning now that it exists.

Waiting on the focused test run (bg_2) before finalizing.

## DEFECT: CHANGELOG says re-archiving clears the restore record; the code never removes it (P3, docs only)

The `Breaking Changes` entry at diff line 18 (`packages/coding-agent/CHANGELOG.md`) says: *"Re-archiving clears that record only when every entry the archive holds has a regular file at its live name — a FIFO, a device or a directory standing there counts as missing — and says which are missing when they are."*

That is the old design. At this head nothing in `gc --archive` deletes the record:
- `copySessionIntoArchive` (`src/cli/gc-cli.ts:2096-2117`) `lstat`s `<archive>.restoring`. When the live tree holds every entry, it only adds the note "this run did not write that record, so it was left … move it aside". Otherwise it adds "was kept; run `omp gc --restore …`". Neither branch calls `unlink` or `rename`.
- Another entry in the same file (diff line 35, `### Fixed`) says the reverse: "`gc --archive` never removes it either".
- The test `archiving a session again leaves a restore record an earlier attempt left, and says so` (`test/session-archive.test.ts:2867`) requires the record's inode and size to be unchanged after `archiveOnly()`. It passed in my run.

**Trigger:** archive a session, do half a restore (`halfRestore()` fixture), make the live tree whole again, then run `gc --archive --apply`. The record is still there, unchanged, and the result's `archive.errors` contains "records a restore that did not finish".

**Impact:** documentation only. A user who reads entry 18 expects re-archiving to clear the marker. In fact `omp --resume <id>` keeps failing until they move `.restoring` aside by hand. **Fix:** drop the "Re-archiving clears that record…" sentence from entry 18, or reword it as "Re-archiving never removes that record, and says which entries are still missing."

## NOT A DEFECT

**Earlier round's findings, checked at this head:**
- **astra #1 / claude's "declared exception" (P1): a forged regular `.restoring` file was deleted. Closed.**
  - `restoreRecordRefusal` (`session-archive.ts:114-132`) no longer reads the file's contents. It only refuses something that isn't a regular file (symlink, FIFO, directory or other), and it uses `lstat`.
  - The record is created with `open(record, "wx")` (`createRestoreRecord`, 175-192). Its dev/ino are taken from that descriptor, and it is rewritten only through the descriptor.
  - `dropOwnRestoreRecord` (208-231) renames the name to a random `.leaving` path. It unlinks that file only when dev/ino match its own record; anything else is put back with `link`.
  - A regular file that was already there means `own === undefined`. It is never written or removed, and the restore reports it with `restoreRecordLeftNote` (2342-2343). `gc --archive` no longer removes it either (gc-cli 2096-2117).
  - Both late-plant races from astra (plant before `wx`, plant before the drop rename) have tests at 4405 and 4433. Both passed.
- **astra #2 (P2): restore forgot a killed live stage when the archived artifact directory was absent. Closed.**
  - `restoreArchivedSessionLocked` now calls `recordedStagingIn(stagingAgentDir, liveArtifacts)` outside the `if (hasArtifacts)` block (2328-2340).
  - The preview's `artifactRestoreConflicts` returns `liveResidue()` when `archiveArtifacts` is missing (1836).
  - Test at 4454 passed: preview and apply both name the stage, `artifactsRestored` is false, the record stays, and the stage bytes are exact.
- **astra #3 (P2, mutable-path boundary): the printed recovery command could stage inside a session tree after its pre-print check. Closed.**
  - `stagingResidueNote` (1731-1769) now prints real paths for the stage and the record.
  - The printed command itself re-resolves both trees with `realpath` after its plain `mkdir`. It runs `rmdir` and exits 1 if the new directory falls inside either tree, or if a tree can't be resolved.
  - Tests at 4471 (sessions tree relinked after the message) and 4503 (agent directory relinked) passed.
- **claude r23:** its other five round-21 items were already marked fixed and nothing at this head undoes them.
  - Its two remaining notes are both addressed. The forged-prefix unlink is gone (see astra #1). On the read-only bucket wording gap, every record message now appends `moveAsidePermission(...)`, which names the `chmod u+w` step.

**Suspicions I ruled out:**
- **Printed `omp gc --restore <timestamp>_<id>` commands** (gc-cli 2115, 2777, 2796) name the whole file stem rather than the bare id. `findArchivedSessionFiles` also matches `name.startsWith(needle)` (session-archive 268), so these commands do resolve.
- **A retry after any failed or killed restore always ends with "record was there before this run" until the user moves it aside.** This is intended: changelog entry 35 says so, the residue note's step 5 tells the user, and the resume test at 2496 covers it.
- **The preview reports a regular record that is already there as an error.** Applying reports the same thing, so the two agree.

**Environment:**
- My first test run failed all 214 tests because my `TMPDIR` directory didn't exist yet (`mkdtemp` ENOENT).
- Rerun: `bun test --timeout 180000 test/session-archive.test.ts` gave **213 pass / 1 fail**, 762 expects, 69 s.
- The one failure, `exporting an archived session yields the same document as live`, threw `Development export viewer not found: …/export-assets/export-viewer-<hash>.js. Run bun gen:export-viewer.` That is a missing generated build asset in the read-only snapshot, not this change.
- I did not run `gc-cli.test.ts`. No typecheck was available.
